extracted.intended_audience: Reviewers and Area Chairs for UAI 2025 (conference peer reviewers / ACs)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and evaluation criteria for reviewers and area chairs handling paper submissions to the UAI 2025 conference, including responsibilities, confidentiality, bidding, formatting and detailed scoring rubrics for reviews and meta-reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness / key dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Please mark these dates in your calendar. Our schedule is tight, so it is key that you respect the deadlines and respond to emails promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists exact deadlines for submission, bidding, review writing, author response, discussion periods, meta-reviews, and notification. Reviewers and ACs must meet these dates (e.g., review writing March 3-24; author notification May 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenReview profile accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure that your OpenReview profile is up to date, since it will be used for assigning submissions to you and to avoid conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you change email address update OpenReview; organizers have no way to know if emails bounced. Accurate profile data avoids misassignment and conflict errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors, Reviewers and ACs will be asked to separately enter two types of conflicts into OpenReview: domain conflicts and individual conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declared conflicts are used to avoid assigning conflicted papers. If you suspect a conflict with an assigned submission, contact the AC (if you are a Reviewer) or Program Chairs (if you are an AC). Do not review if you have an undeclared conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind reviewing policy (reviewer behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewing process is double blind at the level of Reviewers and ACs (Reviewers and ACs cannot see Authors’ identities and vice-versa). Under no circumstances should you attempt to find out the identities of the Authors for any of your assigned submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you accidentally discover Authors’ identities, do not disclose them and do not let them influence your decision in any way (e.g., by searching on Google or arXiv). Reviewers' identities are visible to assigned ACs; AC identities are not visible to Reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of submission materials
rubrics_metrics.description: You agree to keep all material and information confidential (including papers, meta-data, bidding data, messages and discussions related to reviewing, names of committee members, etc.) and use them only for reviewing/area chairing your assigned manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use ideas/results from submissions for your own work or distribute them until publicly available; delete all reviewing material at the end of the cycle (including submitted code). Do not talk about/distribute submissions or reviewing content to anyone without Program Chairs' approval, including other Reviewers/ACs who may have conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author anonymization requirements (violations of double-blind policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must make sure submission (including supplementary material) does not disclose identities or affiliations. Authors should use the third person to refer to their own work, should not include names in acknowledgements, and links that may reveal identities are forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If assigned a submission that is not adequately anonymized, inform the corresponding AC (if you are a Reviewer) or the Program Chairs (if you are an AC) as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting instructions and length limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be formatted using the UAI latex template and formatting instructions. Manuscripts must be submitted as a single PDF file of at most 15 MB. The main part of the manuscript must not exceed 8 pages in length. Unlimited additional pages containing references and appendices are allowed and should be included after the main part in the same file. The appendices should start on a new page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are assigned a paper that is overlength or appears to violate the UAI proceedings format (e.g., decreasing margins or font size), notify the AC (if you are a Reviewer) or the Program Chairs (if you are an AC) as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts that are currently under review or have been accepted or published in a refereed venue with proceedings may not be submitted to UAI. This also applies to substantially identical manuscripts. Submitting to another refereed venue with proceedings while under review at UAI is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conferences/workshops without proceedings, technical report repositories, and arXiv are not considered dual submissions. If you suspect a dual submission, contact the corresponding AC or Program Chairs for clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLMs policy for reviews and meta-reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not allow the use of large language models (LLMs) to write reviews or meta-reviews, except as assistants for checking grammatical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a Reviewer or AC, the responsibility of the text you submit to OpenReview is on you, including any content you write with LLMs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding on submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Bidding on papers that are relevant to your expertise and that you would like to review/area chair is crucial to our process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We will ask you to bid on at least 40 papers with a positive bid so that we can match enough Reviewers/ACs for each paper. Bid on relevant expertise to improve assignment quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area Chairs’ responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs typically oversee around 10 submissions. For each assigned submission, main responsibilities consist of finalizing the list of Reviewers, facilitating the reviewing and discussion process, summarizing it in a meta-review, and providing a recommendation regarding paper acceptance or rejection to the Program Chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May require close reading of the manuscript. ACs will evaluate the quality of each review using three scores: 'exceeds expectations', 'meets expectations', and 'fails to meet expectations'. Top-scoring Reviewers get an honourable mention; lowest-scoring Reviewers may not be invited in future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers typically assess at most 6-7 papers. For each assigned paper, main responsibilities consist of writing constructive and informative reviews, reading the Authors’ responses, participating in the discussions, and providing recommendations regarding acceptance or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide timely, thorough, and polite reviews aimed at helping authors and ACs; engage in discussions, especially for borderline/widely varying assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material handling and size limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions may include further supplementary material (e.g., source code or data) in a ZIP file of up to 50MB that must be separately downloaded from OpenReview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are responsible for reading and reviewing the main part and paying close attention to additional appendices. Looking at further supplementary material (ZIP) is at the Reviewer's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security guidance for executing code / clicking links
rubrics_metrics.description: We cannot provide any guarantees about submitted code and links. Hence, if planning to run supplementary source code, Reviewers should make sure to do this in a secure environment (e.g., Docker, VM, or network-isolated cloud instance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links may contain vulnerabilities or may log visitor IP addresses (thereby revealing your identity). Take precautions (sandboxing/isolation) before running code or following links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author Response / Discussion participation (general guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit responses to their reviews to address concerns and correct misunderstandings, and may interact with Reviewers and ACs during a defined period. Reviewers should read Authors’ responses carefully and with an open mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do the Authors’ comments change your opinion? Read carefully; discussions are led by ACs; be professional, polite, and keep an open mind. You may change your opinion but should not give in to undue influence. Full consensus is not required; different valid conclusions may exist. Focus on borderline papers and widely varying assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q1: Summary and contributions (review content requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please summarize the paper’s motivation and key contributions in a few lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although this may not provide much new information to Authors, it is very valuable to ACs and Program Chairs. (Max. 500 characters.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Q2 overall assessment axes (instruction): originality/novelty, soundness/technical quality, evidence support, clarity, reproducibility, ethical aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Please assess the work along the following axes: originality/novelty, soundness/technical quality, whether claims are supported by convincing evidence, clarity of writing, reproducibility, ethical aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed per-axis scoring guidance is provided below (four-point scales and descriptions). Use these axes to structure Q2 assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / novelty (Q2 axis with 1-4 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: How novel are the concepts, problems addressed, methods introduced, or insights obtained in the paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4 Excellent: main ideas ground-breaking. 3 Good: non-trivial advances. 2 Fair: contributes some new ideas. 1 Poor: not novel or incremental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness / technical quality (Q2 axis with 1-4 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper technically sound?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4 Excellent: confident technically sound, carefully checked details. 3 Good: appears sound but details not carefully checked. 2 Fair: minor, easily fixable technical flaws not impacting main results. 1 Poor: major technical flaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent to which claims are supported by evidence (Q2 axis with 1-4 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the claims supported by convincing evidence (experiments, proofs, code, references, realistic assumptions)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4 Excellent: all claims supported by very convincing evidence (comprehensive eval, rigorous proofs, detailed code, precise refs). 3 Good: main claims supported by convincing evidence. 2 Fair: somewhat supported but evaluation weak or missing baselines, lack of rigor. 1 Poor: fail to convincingly back up main claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility (Q2 axis with 1-4 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the results (theorems, experimental results) in the paper easily reproducible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4 Excellent: key resources (proofs, code, data) available and details comprehensively described for competent researchers to reproduce results. 3 Good: resources available and details sufficiently described. 2 Fair: resources unavailable but details described for an expert to reproduce. 1 Poor: key details incomplete/unclear or resources unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of writing (Q2 axis with 1-4 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper well-organized and clearly written?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4 Excellent: well-organized and clearly written. 3 Good: well-organized but presentation could be improved. 2 Fair: somewhat clear but important details missing or unclear. 1 Poor: unclear and very hard to understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical aspects (Q2 axis / Q10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the submission raise potential ethical concerns (methods, applications, or data that can create/reinforce unfair bias or have primary purpose of harm)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer yes/no and provide brief explanation if yes. This is optional and should not affect the overall rating; its purpose is to flag papers needing further ethical evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q3: Main strengths (review content requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the main strengths of the work, considering the same axes as in Q2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention as many main strengths as there are but avoid minor points here. (Max. 3000 characters.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Q4: Main weaknesses (review content requirement and tone guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the main weaknesses of the work, considering the same axes as in Q2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should be detailed, specific, and polite. Avoid vague/subjective complaints. Do not review your level of interest but its scientific contribution. If calling something incremental, cite specific relevant prior work with full citations. If experiments are unrealistic, suggest concrete improvements. (Max. 3000 characters.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Q5: Detailed comments to the authors (review content requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide constructive criticism and feedback that could help improve the work or its presentation (presentation suggestions, missing references, minor mistakes, typos). You may also include questions to the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want clarifications during author response phase, articulate clearly what you want (e.g., 'I would like to see results of experiment X'). Suggest asking for clarifications only on points important for reaching a decision. (Max. 200000 characters.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Q6: Overall score (1-10 scale with category definitions and distribution guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide your overall evaluation of the paper, carefully weighing reasons to accept and reject. Use full range of scores if appropriate. Do not adjust scores to match conference acceptance rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score choices 10 (Award quality) down to 1 (Very Strong Reject) with detailed descriptions for each score. Guidance on desired distribution: No more than 25% in (Accept + Strong Accept + Very Strong Accept + Award Quality); ≤20% in (Strong Accept + Very Strong Accept + Award Quality); ≤10% in (Very Strong Accept + Award Quality); ≤1% in Award Quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q7: Justification for overall score
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain in a few lines how you arrived at your overall assessment and which aspects you weighted most heavily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Max. 500 characters.) Tie justification back to main strengths and weaknesses (Q3 & Q4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Q8: Confidence in your score (1-5 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate your confidence in your assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5 Very confident (checked all points, expert); 4 Quite confident; 3 Somewhat confident (may have missed details); 2 Not very confident; 1 Not confident (topic outside expertise). Use confidence to inform ACs about how much to rely on your score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q9: Compliance certification
rubrics_metrics.description: I have read the UAI reviewing instructions and certify that I comply with them. In particular, I keep the paper and supplementary materials confidential, and delete all reviewing material at the end of the review cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must explicitly certify compliance when submitting reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and monitoring of reviewer quality by ACs
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs will be asked to evaluate the quality of each review using three scores: 'exceeds expectations', 'meets expectations', and 'fails to meet expectations'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top-scoring Reviewers will get an honourable mention; lowest-scoring Reviewers may not be invited to review at future conferences. ACs should use these assessments when finalizing reviewer selection in future cycles.
